rule.coverage_conditions: Residential rental security deposits under New Jersey's security deposit law; the withholding penalty applies where the tenant receives State or federal financial assistance, including welfare or rental assistance.
rule.penalty: Willful and intentional withholding of a deposit from a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance: civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 per offense. Unlawful use of deposit monies: disorderly persons offense, fine of at least $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both.
rule.quoted_span:
Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on 
behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any Stat e or federal program, 
including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil 
penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

rule.requirement: A landlord or broker may not refuse to rent real property because of the source of any lawful income or lawful rent payment, and may not apply a minimum income or financial standard that is not based exclusively on the tenant's portion of the rent.
rule.key_value: Income standard limited to tenant's portion of rent
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person with the right to sell, rent, lease, assign or sublease any real property, and to real estate brokers and agents; covers all real property, not limited by building age or size.
rule.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age-restricted housing, as to familial status.
rule.penalty: Under the LAD, landlords who violate the law are subject to substantial fines and penalties, up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).
rule.quoted_span: To refuse to sell, rent, lease, assign, or sublease or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons any real property or part or portion thereof because of the source of any lawful income received by the person or the source of any lawful rent payment to be paid for the real property, including, but not limited to, by refusing to accept as payment any source of lawful income or by applying, in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing, any minimum income requirement or financial standard that is not based exclusively on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant; or

sources.quoted_span: To refuse to sell, rent, lease, assign, or sublease or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons any real property or part or portion thereof because of the source of any lawful income received by the person or the source of any lawful rent payment to be paid for the real property, including, but not limited to, by refusing to accept as payment any source of lawful income or by applying, in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing, any minimum income requirement or financial standard that is not based exclusively on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant; or

ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability,

rule.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance annual rent increase cap
rule.requirement: A landlord may not request or receive a rent increase greater than 4% or the CPI-based percentage difference, whichever is less, at lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy. Increases above the allowed amount are void.
rule.key_value: 4% or CPI difference, whichever is less
rule.coverage_conditions: Rental housing spaces in dwellings in Jersey City, except dwellings with four or less housing spaces, licensed hotels/motels, commercial or industrial space, certain new 25+ unit redevelopment dwellings, low rent public housing, and post-October 1, 1983 conversions.
rule.exemptions: Dwellings with four or less housing spaces; licensed hotels or motels; commercial and industrial space; certain new redevelopment dwellings of 25 or more units; low rent public housing; buildings converted to dwelling use on or after October 1, 1983; first rental of a new dwelling or housing space.
rule.penalty: Any rent increase in excess of that authorized is void, and the excess rent must be refunded or credited by the landlord forthwith.
rule.interaction: Clarifies the scope of the state exemption under the New Jersey Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Act; operates within the limitations imposed by the State act (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.6).
rule.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord of any dwelling as defined in § 260-1 may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than four percent or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

sources.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord of any dwelling as defined in § 260-1 may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than four percent or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

registration requirement of Chapter 260.

rule.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in foreclosed properties; month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units are not exempt.
rule.interaction: Federal foreclosure law does not preempt state or local laws giving tenants longer periods or more protections.
rule.quoted_span:
Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units 
must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, 
letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to 
move because of the foreclosure.

rule.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rule.requirement: A rental property owner may not receive or use a coordinator's algorithmic revenue management service, and no person may perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination, including facilitating agreements among landlords that restrict competition on residential rents.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners and coordinators of residential dwelling units in New Jersey; covers any house, apartment or accessory unit used as a primary residence, but not inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities.
rule.exemptions: Coordinating function excludes research/statistical analysis, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, and government affordability controls; government entities are not coordinators; conduct already unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act is unaffected.
rule.penalty: A violation is unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act, and sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73 apply to a violation of section 4.
rule.interaction: Municipalities may not enact ordinances conflicting with the act; the act supplements rather than limits the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
